questions.stem: In isosceles triangle ABC, AB = AC and angle BAC = 80 degrees. Line BD bisects angle ABC and meets AC at D. What is angle BDC?
questions.explanation: Base angles = (180 - 80) / 2 = 50 degrees each. BD bisects angle ABC, so angle DBC = 50 / 2 = 25 degrees. In triangle BDC: angle BCD = 50 degrees and angle DBC = 25 degrees. So angle BDC = 180 - 25 - 50 = 105 degrees.

questions.stem: Can a triangle have sides of length 4 cm, 7 cm, and 12 cm?

options.text: Yes, it forms an obtuse triangle
Yes, it forms an acute triangle

questions.explanation: By the triangle inequality, the sum of any two sides must exceed the third. Here 4 + 7 = 11 < 12, so these lengths cannot form a triangle.

questions.stem: In triangle PQR, side QR is extended to S. Angle QPR = 42 degrees and angle PQR = 75 degrees. What is the exterior angle PRS?
questions.explanation: The exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles: angle PRS = 42 + 75 = 117 degrees.

questions.stem: An equilateral triangle has a perimeter of 24 cm. What is the length of each side?
questions.explanation: An equilateral triangle has all three sides equal. Each side = 24 / 3 = 8 cm.

questions.stem: A triangle has angles 90 degrees, 45 degrees, and 45 degrees. Which of the following best describes this triangle?
questions.explanation: The triangle has a right angle (90 degrees) and two equal angles (45 degrees each), so it has two equal sides. It is a right-angled isosceles triangle.
